title: A passkey campaign switched on by Microsoft
lede: A first-seen service principal created a credential policy and edited another inside one second, scoring 3200 and 2400. Both writes trace to a Microsoft-managed change to the tenant's registration campaign. No person initiated anything.

verdict.text: Microsoft's managed setting retargeted MFA registration from Authenticator to FIDO2. No containment required; expect a tenant-wide wave of passkey enrolments.

grounds.title: Three reasons it looked bad, tested
grounds.intro: No AI-assist verdict was attached; these are the grounds the summaries themselves raise.

items.claim: An unknown service principal wrote an authentication policy.
items.finding: `00000000…` is **Azure Credential Configuration Endpoint Service**, a Microsoft first-party service. It wrote routine MFA-method updates for users all month — 9/1, 9/9, 9/21 — in `Office365`.

It is the backing object for a registration-campaign change written **0.3 s later** in `AzureAuditLogs` by **Microsoft Managed Policy Manager**: target `microsoftAuthenticator` → `Fido2`, snooze 1 → **0**, `Policy.Features` 0 → 16.

items.claim: First time this key or behavior has been seen.
items.finding: The base rate is **1 in 30 days** for any entity on either rule — the shape of a one-off tenant-level rollout, not a campaign of intrusions.

timeline.title: The sequence, from the audit log
timeline.intro: The summaries say 19:40:00. That is the two-minute bucket label; the events below are the raw times.

rows.event: Update policy — **Default Policy**, no properties changed
Authentication Methods Policy Update — campaign target → `Fido2`, all users

items.title: No human policy change.
items.body: Zero user-initiated authentication-policy writes in 30 days; every policy write came from Microsoft-managed identities.

items.title: No methods removed.
items.body: Subsequent writes by the same principal carry empty property diffs.

recommendation: Close benign. Brief analysts that forced passkey registration will fire the AzureAD add-authentication-method rules across the user base; treat that wave as one campaign.
Tell the customer the change was Microsoft-managed. If they do not want enforced passkey registration yet, move the registration campaign off “Microsoft managed” in Entra.

footer.evidence: behavior (2 hits), Office365 (22 rows), AzureAuditLogs (221 rows, 3–4× duplicated)
